title: A violation twice the size that would change a decision raises the shared effect modifier check's alarm rate from 1.3% to 4.5%
question: Population adjustment across a network assumes that a covariate modifies the effect of every active treatment in a class in the same way. There is one published within-network check on that assumption: fit the model with a single interaction shared across the class, refit with treatment-specific interactions one covariate at a time, and compare the posteriors and the model fit. Its authors say it likely has low power. Nobody has measured it, there is no threshold that separates a pass from a failure, and there is no statement of what a pass licenses. Scored against a known truth under a declared distribution of networks, what is it worth?
design: A multilevel network meta-regression with a binomial outcome and a logit link, one individual-level study and the rest aggregate, two active treatments in one class of which only one has individual data. Drift is carried by one covariate and parameterized as the contrast between the two treatments' interactions; a second covariate is shared exactly and supplies a type I error observation from the same fits. 32 cells crossing drift, network size, between-study covariate spread and treatment-effect heterogeneity, 50 replicates each, four fits per replicate forming the complete model lattice, plus eight amendment cells at the decision boundary, a prior-sensitivity arm and an integration-sensitivity check. The target population is not a design factor because the check reads only the fitted network and cannot depend on it; one set of fits is scored at four target displacements, and the reference intercept is solved separately for each so displacement moves the treatment contrast and not the baseline risk.
estimand: Marginal risk difference for the aggregate-only treatment versus the individual-data treatment in a target population, with the population-average conditional log-odds effect as the mechanism scale
methods_compared: check first, then relax exactly what fired
n_sim: 50 per cell, 2,000 networks and 8,960 ML-NMR fits: 6,400 over the 32 registered cells, 1,600 in the amendment arm, 960 in the prior-sensitivity arm. That last arm ran at 30 replicates per cell against the 100 registered, a departure found in round-two review and disclosed in the protocol.
answer: The check does not have the resolution to test the assumption it is read as testing. Against a violation already twice the size that would change a decision, the DIC rule fires in 0.045 [0.029, 0.070] of analyses, against 0.013 [0.005, 0.029] when the assumption holds exactly: a violation that doubles the error that matters moves the alarm rate by about three percentage points. The result does not depend on where the cut is put. Scored threshold-free, the DIC difference ranks a violated network above an intact one with an AUROC of 0.557 [0.517, 0.596] at that violation, so no threshold recovers a ranking the statistic does not contain. The posterior standard deviation of the interaction contrast runs 0.30 to 1.64 against the 0.153 that would make a transported estimate materially wrong, which is why. The equivalence reading, the only one that could confirm rather than merely fail to contradict, fired zero times in 3,200 opportunities, including every replicate where the assumption held exactly; that is a statement about precision, and partly about the prior, since independent normal(0, 2.5) priors already place 0.965 of the contrast beyond the margin. Following the check is still better than not: relaxing exactly what it fires on beats relaxing everything at every target displacement and beats imposing the restriction at every displacement except zero, where the two are indistinguishable.
findings: Detection barely moves with the violation. Pooled over all eight design strata, 400 replicates each, the DIC cut at 5 fires in 0.013 [0.005, 0.029] under the global null, 0.045 [0.029, 0.070] at a contrast of 0.30 that leaves the transported estimate wrong by twice the material threshold, 0.147 at 0.60 and 0.453 at 1.20, which is eight times the decision boundary and a stress test rather than a plausible violation.

The finding survives without any threshold. Scored as a classifier, the DIC difference separates a violated network from an intact one with an AUROC of 0.557 [0.517, 0.596] at a contrast of 0.30, 0.681 [0.644, 0.718] at 0.60 and 0.843 [0.815, 0.870] at 1.20; against material error itself it reaches 0.666 at a target one standard deviation away. This analysis was prespecified, computed from the first run onward, and omitted from the first two drafts until three reviewers asked for it.

The reason is resolution. The posterior standard deviation of the difference between the two treatments' effect modifiers runs 0.30 to 1.64 on the log-odds scale across strata, against 0.153 for the difference that makes the transported estimate materially wrong. An earlier draft led with a prior-removed version of this quantity; its own sensitivity arm showed the quantity is unstable, so the measured posterior standard deviation is what is reported.

The procedure cannot give an all-clear. The equivalence reading, P(|difference| <= 0.153) > 0.95, fired in 0 of 3,200 covariate-checks, including every replicate where the two modifiers were identical by construction. This is a precision result: firing needs a posterior standard deviation below about 0.078 and the tightest stratum reaches 0.30. It is also prior-dependent in the other direction, since independent normal(0, 2.5) priors on the two coefficients put 0.965 of their contrast beyond the margin before any data are seen, above the 0.95 threshold at which the complementary margin rule fires.

The registered verdict fails, and a perfect check would have failed it too. The upper 95% bound on the probability that a passed analysis is materially wrong is 0.697, deployment- weighted, against a registered 0.10. But an oracle that knows the true interaction specification is materially wrong 0.639 of the time on the same replicates, so the check's excess over that oracle is 0.036 and is negative at small target displacements. With a threshold of 0.03 absolute risk, the estimation error of a six-study network alone exceeds it in about half of analyses when the assumption holds exactly. A threshold on total error charges a diagnostic for noise it was never built to detect.

The check is blind to what determines the harm. Its output reads only the fitted network, so its pass rate is identical at every target displacement to the last digit. Over the same fits the probability that a passed analysis is materially wrong rises from 0.427 to 0.723, an excess over the noise floor of 0.296 against a registered 0.20. The first half of that is an algebraic identity that verifies the bookkeeping; the second is empirical.

The three readings are not three procedures. The DIC rule fires without the interval rule in 0.0006 of covariate-checks and the interval rule fires without DIC in 0.106, so the DIC cut is very nearly a strict subset of the interval rule rather than a second opinion. Under the global null they differ in type I error by 0.080 on the drifting covariate and 0.087 pooling both. The 95% interval rule runs at about twice its nominal rate, 0.075 [0.046, 0.120] with no treatment-effect heterogeneity and 0.110 [0.074, 0.161] with it, so avoiding covariate selection does not deliver nominal coverage.
A fire is not a diagnosis. When a violation is present the interval rule fires on the covariate that is shared exactly in up to 0.388 of replicates.

Following the check beats the alternatives, but not uniformly, and the ranking of the alternatives is the surprise. Deployment-weighted and paired on the same replicates, relaxing exactly what fired beats relaxing everything at every displacement on both absolute and squared error, and beats imposing the restriction at displacements 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5 but is indistinguishable from it at 0 (-0.00005, 95% CI [-0.00069, 0.00059]), where there is nothing to transport. Relaxing everything is worse than imposing the restriction, because the relaxed model spends precision the network does not have; it also fails its sampler diagnostics in 0.068 of replicates and 0.24 in the worst cell. The worst diagnostic reached by any model is R-hat 5.13 with effective sample size 1.03, in a singly-relaxed fit.

Knowing the target is worth more than knowing the check statistic. Held out across design factors, the check statistic alone discriminates material error at an AUROC of 0.48 to 0.63, close to chance; adding the target displacement raises it to 0.69 to 0.83. A one-term mapping from the statistic to the probability of material error transports across network size, covariate spread and heterogeneity with absolute errors of 0.013 to 0.058, and fails across drift with an error of 0.469.

On a decision-curve basis, distrusting every adjusted analysis has higher net benefit than every rule in the panel at every action threshold from 0.05 to 0.60. This restates the noise floor rather than measuring the check: with material error present in 0.675 of passing analyses, most of it sampling noise no covariate check can predict, treat-all dominates almost regardless of what the check does.

Two software findings, against multinma 0.9.1.9002 (commit 8489bd83). The package documents class_interactions = 'exchangeable' and raises 'not yet supported', so the hierarchical relaxation this catalog entry proposed as the way forward cannot be fitted; the entry's claim that it ships in the package is wrong for this version. And under the default class_interactions = 'common', an x:.trt term in a regression formula is silently demoted to the class level, so an analyst who follows the published recipe by editing the formula alone fits the shared model twice and can never find evidence against sharing.

Two adversarial critiques before the run found nine issues between them that changed the design, and each found something the other missed. Peer review then found more, including two errors in this study's own code: contraction was divided by the standard deviation of a prior the prior-sensitivity arm was not fitted under, which inverted the reported direction of that arm's result, and the primary bound was a Wilson interval on the unweighted risk printed beside a deployment-weighted point estimate. Both were derived by reviewers from the published numbers alone, without access to the code.
not_answered: The design is a best case in several specific ways that favour the check, and failures attributable to those idealizations are conservative; no general lower-bound claim is made, because three features cut the other way. The true marginal reference risk in the target is supplied to the estimator. Covariates are normal with known target moments and study covariate means are drawn independently of study baselines and of the random treatment effects, so the ecological route identifying the aggregate-only treatment's interaction is unbiased by construction. Conditional constancy holds and only one covariate drifts, linearly. Against that: the fits are fixed-effect while half the cells generate random treatment effects, which is a second specification error that inflates firing; the likelihood is integrated over 64 quadrature points and refitting at 256 changes the DIC verdict in 8.3% of a 24-network subset, which is noise belonging to the implementation and not to the evidence, and 256 points is not demonstrated to be converged; and a single individual-level study is an assumption about the network rather than necessarily a pessimistic one. Beyond that: what a second individual-level study would buy is not measured, that factor having been dropped to pay for treatment-effect heterogeneity. With two active treatments and two covariates, multiplicity across covariates and the selection involved in reading the widest of several pairwise differences are not measured. Where treatment-effect heterogeneity is present the estimand is not cleanly defined, since truth is set at a random effect of zero while a fixed-effect model targets a function of the realized studies; primary results are repeated on the sixteen homogeneous cells and do not change. The hierarchical middle ground between shared and independent interactions could not be fitted because the package does not implement it, and we did not implement it ourselves: that is a reason for its absence, not a justification. The five decision rules scored here are our formalizations of an exploratory published practice, not published rules, and their operating characteristics are ours. Fifty replicates per cell gives a per-cell standard error of 0.065, so nothing is read off a single cell.

reviewers.name: Kimi K3 (via OpenCode)
reviewers.round1: major-revision (late; first attempt returned an empty response, a retry succeeded after round two had been sent, and the report is truncated by an output limit at comment 10)

peer_review.decision: accept with the conclusions narrowed and three limitations recorded
what_review_changed: Two errors in this study's code, both derived by reviewers from published numbers without access to the source: contraction divided by the standard deviation of a prior the prior-sensitivity arm was not fitted under, which inverted the reported direction of that arm's result; and the primary bound computed as a Wilson interval on the unweighted risk while printed beside a deployment-weighted point estimate, 0.777 where the correct weighted bound is 0.697.

The manuscript sent to round two rendered with two literal blanks where amendment-arm results should have been, because a zero-row lookup produced a silent empty string. Reported independently by two reviewers. A publish-time render guard now scans for it and the lookup raises instead of returning nothing.

An undisclosed departure from registration: the prior-sensitivity arm ran at 30 replicates per cell against the 100 registered. Found because a reviewer asked how the published fit count followed from the registered design.

The prespecified AUROC analyses had been computed and then omitted from two drafts. All three reviewers asked for them. They are now the paper's strongest result and the only one resting on no threshold of ours.
Claims the data contradicted, withdrawn: nominal coverage of the credible interval, lowest error at every displacement, and the reported failures being lower bounds in general.

Three defects found while checking the reviewers' arithmetic that no reviewer reported: the worst R-hat was the worst of one model rather than of any model, the paired strategy comparison was unweighted while the RMSE table beside it was weighted, and study.json still carried the title retracted in round one.
not_resolved: Numerical convergence of the 64-point quadrature is unestablished; refitting at 256 points flips the DIC verdict in 8.3% of a 24-network subset and 256 is not shown to be converged. This bounds the primary result and needs a new arm.

Fits that failed their sampler diagnostics remain in the main analysis; the converged-subset sensitivity shows the strategy ranking does not depend on them but does not make a DIC from a chain with R-hat 5.13 usable.
The exchangeable, partial-pooling comparator is absent because the package does not implement it and we did not write it.
peer_review.process_note: Revision two was not sent back to the reviewers. It changed two code paths and several published numbers, and this decision is made on a version no reviewer saw. That is a weakness of a two-round protocol when the second round finds bugs rather than overstatements.
